Simulate BOIN12 Trials

Source: R/boin12_simulate.R
boin12_simulate.Rd

Simulate trials of the BOIN12 design of Lin et al. (2020), which assigns each cohort to the most desirable dose by a utility that weighs the response against the DLT, and return the patients, DLTs and responses at every dose. This is the simulation engine behind sim_boin12.

Usage

boin12_simulate(
  target,
  target_resp,
  p_true,
  p_resp,
  n_cohort,
  cohort_size,
  n_trials = 10000,
  start_dose = 1,
  n_earlystop = NULL,
  n_earlystop_rule = c("with_stay", "simple"),
  p_saf = NULL,
  p_tox = NULL,
  cutoff_eli = 0.95,
  cutoff_eli_resp = 0.9,
  psi00 = 40,
  psi11 = 60,
  benchmark_weight = 0.5,
  utility_prior = c(1, 1),
  n_star = 6,
  n_explore = 9,
  tie_break = c("higher", "random"),
  no_candidate = c("nearest", "stop"),
  explore_from = c("any", "admissible"),
  resp_cor = 0,
  resp_cor_type = c("copula", "binary"),
  seed = 123
)

Arguments

target

Numeric scalar. Highest acceptable DLT probability, called phi_T by Lin et al. (2020). It is the target of the BOIN boundaries lambda_e and lambda_d, of the admissibility of a dose and of the MTD that bounds the OBD. Lin et al. recommend a value slightly above the target of a design that only considers toxicity, for example 0.35 instead of 0.30.

target_resp

Numeric scalar. Lowest acceptable response probability, phi_E. Note that this is a lower limit, as in sim_bf_boin_et, whereas the target_resp of sim_boin_et is a target.

p_true

Numeric vector. True DLT probability at each dose.

p_resp

Numeric vector. True response probability at each dose.

n_cohort

Integer scalar. Number of cohorts in a trial.

cohort_size

Integer scalar or vector. Number of patients per cohort. A scalar is used for every cohort; a shorter vector is padded with its last element.

n_trials

Integer scalar. Number of trials to simulate. Defaults to 10000.

start_dose

Integer scalar. Dose level of the first cohort. Defaults to 1.

n_earlystop

Integer scalar or NULL. Number of patients at the current dose that ends the trial when the next cohort would stay there (see n_earlystop_rule). Defaults to NULL, which runs every trial to the maximum sample size, as in Lin et al. (2020).

n_earlystop_rule

Character scalar. "with_stay" (the default) ends the trial at n_earlystop only when the next cohort would stay at the current dose, as in the example of Zhou et al. (2022); "simple" ends it in any case.

p_saf, p_tox

Numeric scalars or NULL. Highest DLT probability deemed subtherapeutic and lowest deemed overly toxic, which give the BOIN boundaries. Default to 0.6 * target and 1.4 * target.

cutoff_eli

Numeric scalar. A dose is inadmissible, together with every higher dose, when the posterior probability that its DLT rate exceeds target is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.95.

cutoff_eli_resp

Numeric scalar. A dose is inadmissible when the posterior probability that its response rate is below target_resp is at least this cutoff. Defaults to 0.90.

psi00, psi11

Numeric scalars from 0 to 100. Utility of a patient without DLT and without response, and with both. The utility of a response without DLT is 100 and that of a DLT without response is 0. Default to 40 and 60, the example of Lin et al. (2020).

benchmark_weight

Numeric scalar above 0 and at most 1. The utility benchmark is benchmark_weight * u_low + (1 - benchmark_weight) * 100, where u_low is the expected utility of a dose whose DLT and response probabilities are target and target_resp, the two outcomes being independent. Defaults to 0.5, the benchmark of Lin et al. (2020); Lu et al. (2025) use 0.6.

utility_prior

Numeric vector of two positive numbers. Beta prior of the utility of a dose divided by 100. Defaults to c(1, 1).

n_star

Integer scalar. With at least this many patients at the current dose and a DLT rate between lambda_e and lambda_d, the next dose is chosen from the current dose and the dose below. Defaults to 6.

n_explore

Integer scalar. With at least this many patients at the current dose, a DLT rate below lambda_d and an untried admissible dose above, the next cohort goes to that dose. Defaults to 9.

tie_break

Character scalar. Choice among the doses of equal desirability: "higher" (the default) takes the highest of them, the rule of the BOIN12 software according to the 'escalation' package; "random" takes one of them at random, as stated in Table S2 of the Supplement of Lin et al. (2020). See Details.

no_candidate

Character scalar. What happens when none of the doses allowed for the next cohort is admissible: "nearest" (the default) goes to the admissible dose nearest to the current one; "stop" ends the trial without an OBD. See Details.

explore_from

Character scalar. Doses from which the exploration rule (see n_explore) escalates: "any" (the default) from any dose, as in the 'escalation' package; "admissible" only from an admissible dose, as the results published by Lin et al. (2020) indicate. See Details.

resp_cor

Numeric scalar between -1 and 1. Correlation between the DLT and the response of a patient, see resp_cor_type. Defaults to 0.

resp_cor_type

Character scalar. "copula" (the default) links the two outcomes by a Gaussian copula with correlation resp_cor, the bivariate normal model of Lin et al. (2020); "binary" sets the correlation of the two binary outcomes, as in boin_et_simulate.

seed

Integer scalar or NULL. Random seed. The state of the calling session is restored on exit. Defaults to 123.

Value

An object of class boin12_trials, which is a list with components

n_pts, n_tox, n_resp, n_tox_resp

Integer matrices, one row per trial and one column per dose, of the patients treated, the DLTs, the responses and the patients with both a DLT and a response.

cohorts_used

Integer vector of the cohorts enrolled.

stop_reason

Character vector: "no_admissible_dose", "n_earlystop", "max_cohorts" or "no_admissible_candidate" (only with no_candidate = "stop").

early_stop

Logical vector, TRUE for the trials stopped because no dose was admissible or, with no_candidate = "stop", because no dose allowed for the next cohort was admissible. These trials select no OBD.

design

"BOIN12".

boundary

List with lambda_e, lambda_d, u_low and u_benchmark.

settings

List of the design parameters.

Details

After each cohort, with phat the DLT rate at the current dose: the trial stops when no dose is admissible; when n_explore patients have been treated at the current dose, phat is below lambda_d and the dose above is untried, the dose is escalated (with explore_from = "admissible", only when the current dose is admissible); otherwise, when phat is at least lambda_d, the next dose is the highest admissible dose below the current one (the current one if there is none); when phat is above lambda_e and at least n_star patients have been treated, the next dose is the more desirable of the current dose and the dose below; otherwise it is the most desirable of the dose below, the current dose and the dose above. Only admissible doses are considered. Ties go to the higher dose, as in the BOIN12 software according to the 'escalation' package, or with tie_break = "random" to one of the tied doses drawn at random. When none of these doses is admissible, the admissible dose nearest to the current one is chosen, ties to the lower dose. The desirability is that of boin12_decision_table.

With no_candidate = "stop", the trial stops instead, without an OBD and with the stopping reason "no_admissible_candidate", when none of these doses is admissible and when phat is at least lambda_d and no dose below the current one is admissible. At the lowest dose, a phat of at least lambda_d still keeps the next cohort there when that dose is admissible.

Lin et al. (2020) leave three points open, decided here as follows. A dose made inadmissible by its DLT data also makes every higher dose inadmissible, as in BOIN and in Lu et al. (2025), whereas the 'escalation' package only checks the doses next to the current one. A de-escalation never goes to an inadmissible dose; 'escalation' moves to the dose below whatever its data. The trial stops when no dose is admissible; 'escalation' goes on at the lowest dose when its DLT rate is high. The article breaks ties at random; the software chooses the higher dose. tie_break = "random", no_candidate = "stop" and explore_from = "admissible" are the settings compared with the results published by Lin et al. (2020) in inst/reproduce/reproduce_Lin2020.R; the last two rules are not stated in the article and were inferred from those results.

Each patient draws two uniform variates in enrollment order, the first for the DLT and the second for the response. With tie_break = "random", a decision among tied doses draws one more variate, so that the trials depart from those with "higher" after the first tie.

References

Lin, R., Zhou, Y., Yan, F., Li, D. and Yuan, Y. (2020). BOIN12: Bayesian optimal interval phase I/II trial design for utility-based dose finding in immunotherapy and targeted therapies. JCO Precision Oncology, 4, 1393-1402. doi:10.1200/PO.20.00257

Zhou, Y., Lin, R., Lee, J. J., Li, D., Wang, L., Li, R. and Yuan, Y. (2022). TITE-BOIN12: A Bayesian phase I/II trial design to find the optimal biological dose with late-onset toxicity and efficacy. Statistics in Medicine, 41(11), 1918-1931. doi:10.1002/sim.9337

Lu, M., Zhang, J., Yuan, Y. and Lin, R. (2025). Comb-BOIN12: A utility-based Bayesian optimal interval design for dose optimization in cancer drug-combination trials. Statistics in Biopharmaceutical Research, 17(2), 266-276. doi:10.1080/19466315.2024.2370403

Examples

# Scenario 1 of Lin et al. (2020)
trials <- boin12_simulate(
  target = 0.35, target_resp = 0.25,
  p_true = c(0.05, 0.12, 0.27, 0.35, 0.50),
  p_resp = c(0.20, 0.35, 0.36, 0.37, 0.38),
  n_cohort = 12, cohort_size = 3, n_trials = 200, seed = 123
)
trials
#> Simulated BOIN12 trials
#>   trials               : 200
#>   doses                : 5
#>   DLT limit            : 0.35
#>   response limit       : 0.25
#>   cohorts              : 12 of size 3
#>   max sample size      : 36
#> 
#> Average per trial:
#>                     DL1   DL2  DL3  DL4  DL5
#> Patients treated   8.18 12.38 8.30 5.10 2.06
#> DLTs observed      0.47  1.44 2.19 1.88 1.03
#> Responses observed 1.79  4.23 3.02 1.85 0.81
#> 
#> Stopping reason (%):
#> 
#> max_cohorts 
#>         100
